A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same study, with matching authors, methods, and MultiClaim data. Their main text and appendices are readable, and results can be matched across renumbering, relocation, and revised displays.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendices B–C report original retrieval, reranking, and fine-tuning experiments, including S@10 and MRR@10 results.

after.justification: Retains those original experiments and adds English-excluded, language-specific, translation, and correlation results in Section 6 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The dense retrieval, cross-encoder and RankGPT reranking, and offline random/topic/similarity negative-sampling procedures remain unchanged, as does the training loss. The added translation experiment is a comparator rather than a revision of the proposed original-language approach.

E1.justification: The MultiClaim subset, 47 languages, and 283 language combinations are retained. v2 extends evaluation scenarios within this corpus through English-excluded retrieval, English/Hindi monolingual versus crosslingual breakdowns, and English-translated inputs.

E2.justification: The existing embedding models, rerankers, and negative-sampling comparators remain. Appendix D newly evaluates translating posts and fact-checks into English before unsupervised multilingual-e5-large retrieval; v1 discusses translation literature but does not report this comparator.

E3.justification: New evaluation procedures exclude pairs containing English on either side, leaving 118 crosslingual test pairs, separately score English/Hindi monolingual and crosslingual pairs, and evaluate translated inputs. Original split counts, both metrics, top-30 reranking, and supervised training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens the diagnostic analyses beyond v1's negative-count curves and retrieval/reranking comparisons. It adds English-exclusion controls, English/Hindi breakdowns, correlations between model capacity and performance, and a translation comparison investigating sensitivity to input language.

E5.justification: v2 Table 8 introduces Pearson correlations and associated p-values for embedding dimensions and parameter counts versus MRR@10. Both versions already report three-seed averages and standard deviations for supervised results; no increased run count is reported.

E6.justification: Tables 5–6 retain their numerical scores, but v2 adds substantial subgroup, correlation, and translation results. Appendix D reports translated E5 crosslingual MRR@10 of 0.6017 and S@10 of 0.7514. Some redisplayed values also change inconsistently: Linq-Embed-Mistral's crosslingual S@10 changes from 0.3292 in v1 Figure 3 to 0.3929 in v2 Figure 6, although Table 6 retains 0.3292.

T1.justification: The ranking-problem formulation is unchanged. No new mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs appear; the added correlation analysis is empirical statistical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central claims about LLM reranking, negative sampling, and distinctive crosslingual behavior. The introduction newly claims that separating both posts and fact-checks across splits addresses contamination overlooked by prior work, explicitly positioning the released subset and splits as an additional contribution.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 now foregrounds MRR@10 and recognizes cross-encoder reranking's advantage over fine-tuning for crosslingual ranking quality. New discussion attributes greater importance to data and pretraining than model capacity or architecture, while Appendix D qualifies translation's usefulness by linguistic setting. The existing dataset limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: v1 promises code and data upon acceptance; v2 states public availability and supplies a repository link. Section 3 and Appendix A distinguish an initial 200-post threshold from the final 180-post cutoff and explain the motivation for the already documented language-detection ensemble. Hardware and hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Peng et al. (2025) SemEval overview citation, explicitly positions contamination-aware splits as a contribution, and contrasts its translation findings with Pikuliak et al. (2023). Other reference changes largely update bibliographic details for existing works.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, research questions, and main section order remain. Copyediting, fuller model names, and localized rewrites emphasize MRR@10 in the results discussion. Appendix C's subsections are consolidated, and Appendix D is added.

P2.justification: The result displays are substantially reorganized: Figure 3 becomes a three-panel MRR@10 comparison, and MRR@10/S@10 displays exchange main-text and appendix roles. v1 Table 8 becomes expanded v2 Table 2, while v1 Table 3 becomes expanded v2 Table 9. v2 also adds language-specific and correlation tables, redraws Figure 1, and reformats benchmark tables.

improvement.justification: The new language controls and translation baseline make the approaches' applicability more assessable, while the release link and preprocessing clarification improve reproducibility documentation. These provide a limited net gain over v1's already extensive evidence. Benefits are tempered by new chart/table discrepancies, such as Figure 6 versus Table 6, and overly strong conclusions about capacity and architecture drawn from nonsignificant correlations.
